clue.text: Best at everything, including standing

indicators.note: the phrase Best at everything is said to include the word, so it sits inside those letters

explanation.surface: A boast about someone who excels at everything, including their social position.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the old sense: one's estate is one's rank or condition in life, one's standing.

clue.text: Picture would be offensive if former pupil was present

indicators.note: the clue says the offensive word arises only if the old boy were there, so the picture is that word with him taken away

parts.note: something that would be offensive is indecent or lewd
OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a British school

explanation.surface: An image that would cause offence if an old schoolboy were in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: adding OB to the answer would give a word for offensive, so the answer is that word minus OB.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a scene is a view or picture, as in a painted landscape.

clue.text: They make up everything — most are fake

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of land area, abbreviated A

indicators.note: fake means counterfeit or made up, so these letters are reworked into another order

explanation.surface: A cynic's remark that people invent everything and most of them are frauds.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the old joke 'never trust these, they make up everything'. 'fake' rearranges MOST plus A, the abbreviation for the area unit are.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal sense of the pun: all matter is composed of these tiny particles.

clue.text: Passed wind, asleep and sedated at last

indicators.note: to wind is to twist or coil, so the letters of asleep are twisted into a new order
at last points to the final letter of the word sedated

explanation.surface: A rather rude hospital scene: someone breaks wind while sedated and asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed wind' reads as one phrase, but 'Passed' is the definition and 'wind' turns ASLEEP into ELAPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: time that has passed has gone by.

clue.text: Essentially, Colin 'Sex Appeal' Firth encapsulates virtue

indicators.note: to encapsulate is to enclose, so the Scottish inlet holds the other letters

parts.note: the Moray Firth is a large inlet on the north-east coast of Scotland

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its centre, so take the middle letter of Colin

parts.note: IT is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Tabloid gossip about Colin Firth, the actor famed for sex appeal, being a model of virtue.
explanation.walkthrough: Colin Firth is the actor, but here Firth means a Scottish sea inlet, the Moray Firth.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: morality is moral goodness, virtuous conduct.

clue.text: In France, my sister overheard person trying to relax

indicators.note: overheard means the French phrase is caught by ear, so its sound gives the letters entered

parts.note: my sister in French is ma soeur

explanation.surface: Someone eavesdrops in France on their sister, who is trying to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'person trying to relax' reads as someone unwinding, but means someone working to relax a client.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a masseur gives massages, trying to make the client's muscles relax.

clue.text: Told off leader — About time!

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or bad, so the letters of leader plus time are muddled

explanation.surface: Someone reprimands their boss and exclaims that it was long overdue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Told off' reads as one phrase; 'Told' is the definition and 'off' signals mixing LEADER with T, with 'About' as a further hint of turning around.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to relate a story is to tell or recount it.

clue.text: A tie with a perfect result: 0-0 draw?

definitions.text: A tie with a perfect result
definitions.meaning: a tie is a marriage, and the perfect one is a union made for love
a nil-nil game in tennis scoring terms, love all

explanation.surface: A sports report about a tied game ending scoreless.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis, love means zero, so a game ending 0-0 would be a match of love.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage made for love rather than money, and punningly a game with no score.

clue.text: Swears to check whether that is special

parts.note: to check something is to test it
if can mean whether, as in ask if it rains
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Someone swears to verify whether a thing is really special.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a witness under oath swears to a fact, declaring it in court.

clue.text: Eccles sent back former Israeli leader to get symbols of Judaism

parts.note: the setter is Eccles, so in the setter's voice that is ME

indicators.note: something sent back is returned, so the name is read in reverse

parts.note: Ariel Sharon was Prime Minister of Israel 2001-2006

explanation.surface: The setter returns a former Israeli prime minister in exchange for religious emblems.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's name stands for ME or I.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the seven- or nine-branched candelabrum is one of the best-known emblems of the Jewish faith.

clue.text: Extravagant, like John?

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, and lav (lavatory) is British slang for the same
the suffix -ish means like or somewhat, as in childish

explanation.surface: Asking whether some John is a big spender.
explanation.walkthrough: John looks like a person's name, but it is the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lavish spending is extravagant, generous to excess.

clue.text: Long-lasting prettiness requires surgery

indicators.note: surgery reshapes something, so the letters of prettiness are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cynical claim that lasting good looks need cosmetic surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something persistent continues, enduring over a long time.

clue.text: Periodically misadvised servant

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so take every third letter of misadvised

explanation.surface: A domestic servant who keeps being given bad advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a maid is a female domestic worker.

clue.text: It destroys evidence Republican got rid of boxes with Communist revolutionary

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so the discarding word holds the party letter

parts.note: to shed is to get rid of
R is the abbreviation for a US Republican

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning round, so the word for communist is reversed

parts.note: a red is a communist

explanation.surface: A Republican hides evidence in boxes with a communist revolutionary's help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Communist revolutionary' reads as one figure, but 'revolutionary' turns RED to DER.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an office machine that cuts documents into strips, getting rid of paper evidence.

clue.text: Polish cult founder conceals yen to take holiday following hitch

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide inside, so the polishing and founder words surround the currency letter

parts.note: to hone is to sharpen or polish
Sun Myung Moon founded the Unification Church, whose followers are called Moonies
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A Polish religious leader hides money before a trip that hits a snag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like a nationality but is the verb. 'hitch' means getting hitched, i.e. married.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: newly-weds take this holiday right after the wedding.

clue.text: I simpered dreadfully in thin outer layer

indicators.note: done dreadfully means done badly, so the letters of I simpered are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone simpered awkwardly while sounding thin and superficial.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomical term: the outermost layer of skin, a thin protective covering.

clue.text: Destroyed leaves? Definitely not — see over for the finer points

indicators.note: see over is a page instruction to turn, so the remaining letters are read backwards
not says the word for definitely is to be excluded

parts.note: defoliated means stripped of leaves
defo is British slang for definitely

explanation.surface: A note about foliage being destroyed, with a pointer to read the small print overleaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Definitely not' reads as an emphatic denial, but removes DEFO, leaving LIATED; 'see over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: detail means the small particulars, the finer points of something.

clue.text: Rub guano into shoulders

indicators.note: to shoulder is to carry, so the phrase guano into carries the word inside it

explanation.surface: Gardening or grooming advice: massage bird droppings into the shoulders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoulders' looks like body parts but is a verb meaning carries.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to anoint is to smear or rub with oil, often ceremonially.

clue.text: Bottom fan, or breast? An initially intriguing answer

parts.note: tit is slang for a breast

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about whether someone admires bottoms or breasts.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, the fairy queen falls in love with Bottom the weaver.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary allusion: under a spell, the fairy queen dotes on the weaver Bottom, making her his fan.

clue.text: Trump starts to harass emigrants, sending them the greatest distance possible

parts.note: trump is British slang for breaking wind

indicators.note: starts to points to the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Donald Trump harassing migrants and sending them as far away as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump is the president in the surface, but British slang for breaking wind in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative: to the greatest distance is to go as far as possible.

clue.text: That woman ran outside, wounded

indicators.note: outside says the running word goes round the pronoun

parts.note: fled means ran away
that woman is she

explanation.surface: A woman ran outside after being hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunting sense: a fleshed blade or wound has cut into flesh.

clue.text: Is bitter about topless hosts

indicators.note: topless means losing the top, so the first letter of the word for hosts goes

parts.note: a host presents a show

explanation.surface: Someone resentful about hosts who go without tops.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to resent something is to feel bitter about it.

clue.text: Kind face

definitions.meaning: a kind or sort of thing

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a category or sort, and the printing term for a typeface.

clue.text: Moneymen certain to be involved in disgraceful arrest

indicators.note: involved in means placed within, so the word for certain goes inside the jumbled letters
disgraceful suggests something in a sorry state, so the letters of arrest are scrambled

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: Financial officers are sure to be caught up in a scandalous arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disgraceful' looks like a comment on the arrest but makes TREARS; 'to be involved in' sends the word for certain into that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: officials who manage an organisation's funds, so men handling money.

clue.text: Half of football team is dismissed in Spain, for example

indicators.note: half of says only the first five of the ten letters are kept

parts.note: Real Madrid is a famous Spanish football club

explanation.surface: Half a football side is sent off during a match in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is dismissed' says the other half goes, leaving REALM.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Spain is a kingdom, and a kingdom is a realm.

clue.text: Make speech naked for one-to-one?

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters go

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A dare to give a speech in the nude, perhaps in a private session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-to-one' suggests a private meeting, but here it is the proportion 1:1.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one-to-one, written 1:1, is a proportion comparing two quantities.

clue.text: Perhaps Michael Gove is a fraud

definitions.meaning: Gove, a Conservative politician, is an example of a Tory man

explanation.surface: A political jibe calling a Conservative cabinet minister a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Gove was a senior Conservative minister; CON is the abbreviation for Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a Conservative male, and a swindler who tricks people.

clue.text: Eager to embrace new plans, primarily, for pre-match gathering

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within, so the word for eager wraps around the other letters

parts.note: hearty means eager or enthusiastic

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of plans

explanation.surface: Someone keen to adopt new plans before a big game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pre-match' suggests sport, but the match is a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a celebration held for a bride shortly before her wedding.

clue.text: Tattoos and bronze originally done well with pens

parts.note: to ink someone is to tattoo them
a bronze is a tan

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of done

explanation.surface: Praise for tattoos and a bronzed body, nicely done with pens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done well' reads as praise, but 'well' joins the definition: an ink well.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a desk stand holding an ink pot and pens.

clue.text: Criminal mob with sly character

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of mob and sly are bent into new order

explanation.surface: A gangster group accompanied by a cunning individual.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a character is a written sign such as a letter or mark.
